title: 99. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Speed as Distance per Unit Time
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Speed as Distance per Unit Time
questions.learningObjective: Calculate average speed from given distance and time.
questions.question: A car travels \(120\text{ km}\) in \(2\) hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed is distance divided by time. Here, \(120 \div 2 = 60\), so the average speed is \(60\text{ km/h}\). The choice "\(240\text{ km/h}\)" is the product of distance and time, not the speed.

questions.concept: Speed as Distance per Unit Time
questions.learningObjective: Calculate average speed from given distance and time.
questions.question: A cyclist travels \(45\text{ km}\) in \(3\) hours. What is the average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed is total distance divided by total time: \(\frac{45}{3}=15\text{ km/h}\). The alternative uses \(2\) hours instead of the stated \(3\), since \(\frac{45}{2}=22.5\).
questions.hint: Divide the total distance by the total time.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate average speed when distance is in metres and time is in seconds.
questions.question: A runner covers \(400\text{ m}\) in \(50\) seconds. What is the average speed in metres per second?
questions.explanation: Average speed is distance divided by time. Here, \(400 \div 50 = 8\), so the average speed is \(8\text{ m/s}\). The choice "\(0.125\text{ m/s}\)" is the reciprocal \(50 \div 400\), which reverses the relationship.
questions.hint: Use \(\text{speed} = \text{distance} \div \text{time}\) with the given metres and seconds.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate average speed when the time is given as a decimal number of hours.
questions.question: A train travels \(180\text{ km}\) in \(1.5\) hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed is distance divided by time. Here, \(180 \div 1.5 = 120\), so the average speed is \(120\text{ km/h}\). The choice "\(270\text{ km/h}\)" is the product \(180 \times 1.5\), which is not the speed.
questions.hint: Divide the distance by the time in hours, including the decimal part.

questions.learningObjective: Determine distance travelled at a constant speed.
questions.question: A car travels \(150\text{ km}\) in \(3\) hours. At the same average speed, how far will it travel in \(5\) hours?
questions.explanation: First find the average speed: \(150 \div 3 = 50\text{ km/h}\). Then multiply by the new time: \(50 \times 5 = 250\text{ km}\). The choice "\(300\text{ km}\)" would correspond to an average speed of \(60\text{ km/h}\).
questions.hint: Find the speed for one hour first, then multiply by \(5\) hours.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate average speed when the time is given as a decimal number of hours.
questions.question: An airplane flies \(1800\text{ km}\) in \(2.25\) hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed is distance divided by time. Here, \(1800 \div 2.25 = 800\), so the average speed is \(800\text{ km/h}\). The choice "\(900\text{ km/h}\)" ignores the quarter-hour and calculates \(1800 \div 2\).
questions.hint: Divide the distance by the full time in hours, including the decimal part.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate distance travelled when speed and time are given.
questions.question: A cyclist rides at an average speed of \(12\text{ km/h}\) for \(2.5\) hours. How far does the cyclist travel?
questions.explanation: Distance is speed multiplied by time. Here, \(12 \times 2.5 = 30\), so the cyclist travels \(30\text{ km}\). The choice "\(14.5\text{ km}\)" is the sum \(12 + 2.5\), which is not the distance.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate average speed when the time is given as a decimal number of hours.
questions.question: A boat travels \(84\text{ km}\) in \(3.5\) hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed is \(\frac{84}{3.5}=24\text{ km/h}\). The alternative drops the half-hour and calculates \(\frac{84}{3}=28\).
questions.hint: Divide the distance by the time in hours, including the decimal part.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a mixed time unit to hours and then calculate average speed.
questions.question: A car travels \(210\text{ km}\) in \(2\) hours \(20\) minutes. What is its average speed in \(\text{km/h}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert \(20\) minutes to hours: \(20 \div 60 = \frac{1}{3}\) hour, so the total time is \(2 + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{7}{3}\) hours. Then \(210 \div \frac{7}{3} = 210 \times \frac{3}{7} = 90\). Thus the average speed is \(90\text{ km/h}\). The choice "\(105\text{ km/h}\)" would result from using only \(2\) hours.
questions.hint: Convert minutes to hours before dividing distance by time.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the time needed to travel a given distance at a constant speed.
questions.question: A train travels \(300\text{ km}\) in \(2.5\) hours. At the same average speed, how long will it take to travel \(480\text{ km}\)?
questions.explanation: First find the average speed: \(300 \div 2.5 = 120\text{ km/h}\). Then the time for \(480\text{ km}\) is \(480 \div 120 = 4\) hours. The choice "\(5\) hours" would correspond to a slower speed.
questions.hint: Find the speed first, then use \(\text{time} = \text{distance} \div \text{speed}\).
